stem: What does tracing add to an LLM application beyond ordinary logs?

options.text: A linked view of each request across retrieval, prompts, model calls and tools with timings and token counts

explanation: Traces connect the steps of one request so you can see where latency, cost or errors arise and reproduce problems.

stem: Why should prompts and model versions be version-controlled and deployed through a controlled pipeline?

options.text: Behaviour changes with them, so changes must be reviewable, testable against evaluations and reversible

explanation: Prompts and model choices are part of the system behaviour. Treat them like code: review, test, version and roll back.

stem: Which signals are most useful to monitor in production for a RAG assistant?

options.text: Latency, cost, error and refusal rates, retrieval hit quality indicators, user feedback and sampled quality reviews

explanation: Quality, cost and reliability must all be observed, ideally with sampled human review, since automatic metrics miss some failures.

stem: Prompt changes are edited directly in production by two engineers. Last week an edit silently increased refusals; nobody knows which change caused it.

options.text: Store prompts in version control, require review and an automated evaluation run before release, deploy through a pipeline with versioned releases and a quick rollback, and monitor refusal rate after release.
Ask engineers to message each other before editing.
Log the final prompt text only.

rationales.text: Versioning and review provide traceability for behaviour changes.
Automated evaluation catches regressions before users do.
Freezing removes the need to improve the assistant.

explanation: Without version control, evaluation gating and rollback, behaviour changes cannot be attributed or undone. Treat prompts as release artefacts.
model_answer: Put prompts in version control, add review and automated evaluation gates, release with versions, enable rollback, and monitor key metrics after release.

stem: Leadership asks how the team knows the assistant is still giving good answers six months after launch, when documents and user questions have changed.
constraints: Cost of full review is high

options.text: Set up ongoing monitoring: sampled, rubric-based human review of production conversations, automated checks, drift indicators on questions and retrieval results, and periodic refresh of the evaluation set.
Rely on the launch-day test results.

rationales.text: Launch tests remain valid regardless of content change.
Evaluation sets need refreshing as usage drifts.
Complaints alone give early warning for silent quality loss.

explanation: Quality drifts as content and questions change. Continuous sampled review, automated checks and a refreshed evaluation set provide affordable assurance.
model_answer: Define quality rubrics, sample production traffic for review, track drift signals, refresh evaluation data, and review trends regularly.

rubric.criterion: Drift or refresh of evaluation data
